title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (EU AI Act) — Annex III, High-Risk AI Systems
publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
summary: Binding EU regulation. Annex III classifies AI systems used for medical diagnosis, triage, treatment recommendation, and other health-related consequential decisions as 'high-risk', triggering conformity assessment, risk management, data governance, human oversight, and post-market monitoring duties on providers and deployers.

title: Digital Omnibus on AI — provisional agreement postponing Annex III high-risk obligations
publisher: European Commission / Council of the EU / European Parliament (trilogue)
summary: Amends the EU AI Act's compliance calendar. Annex III (use-based) high-risk obligations are postponed from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, except AI already regulated as a medical device under the Medical Device Regulation (MDR) or In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR) requiring Notified Body assessment, which must still comply by August 2026/2027.

title: HIPAA Privacy Rule and Security Rule (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164)
publisher: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services (HHS)
summary: Federal law. Applies in full, without modification, to any AI system that accesses, processes, stores, or transmits electronic protected health information (ePHI) — including ePHI used in AI training data, prediction models, and algorithm outputs.

title: Affordable Care Act Section 1557 Nondiscrimination Rule
publisher: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights (HHS OCR)
summary: Binding federal nondiscrimination rule, explicitly extended by OCR to cover AI-based 'patient care decision support tools.' Covered entities must identify tools that use race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability as input variables and mitigate resulting discrimination risk.

title: Colorado Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 24-205, re-enacted by SB 26-189)
summary: State law effective 30 June 2026 regulating developers and deployers of 'high-risk AI systems' that make or are a substantial factor in consequential decisions in healthcare (and other sectors). Requires reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination, annual impact assessments, and consumer disclosures.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (Draft Guidance)
summary: Non-binding FDA draft guidance covering the total product lifecycle (TPLC) of AI-enabled Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), including recommendations for marketing submissions, performance monitoring, and user-facing transparency.

title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP) for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions
summary: Final FDA guidance describing how manufacturers of AI-enabled medical devices can pre-specify planned, controlled model changes (recalibration, retraining) in a marketing submission rather than requiring a new submission for every update.

title: Ensuring Nondiscrimination Through the Use of Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies (Guidance)
summary: OCR guidance operationalizing Section 1557 for AI: covered entities should know what input variables a clinical AI tool uses, obtain training-data information from vendors, train staff to spot discriminatory outputs, and keep a human able to override the tool.

title: Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health: WHO Guidance
summary: First global normative guidance on AI ethics in health. Establishes six core principles: protect autonomy; promote human well-being and safety; ensure transparency and explainability; foster accountability; ensure inclusiveness and equity; promote responsive, sustainable AI.

title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS)
summary: World's first certifiable AI-specific management-system standard. Requires organizations to implement AI risk management, AI system impact assessments, lifecycle management, and third-party/vendor-model oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: Voluntary, sector-agnostic framework structured around four functions — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage — for identifying and managing AI risk across the system lifecycle. Widely used as a baseline for healthcare AI risk programs.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile, NIST AI 600-1
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: Companion profile to the AI RMF identifying risks unique to generative AI (confabulation, data leakage, over-reliance) and recommended actions — directly relevant to patient-facing generative AI chatbots and clinical-note-generation tools.

title: Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP) for Medical Device Development — 10 Guiding Principles
publisher: International Medical Device Regulators Forum (IMDRF); endorsed by FDA/Health Canada/MHRA
summary: Multi-regulator consensus principles covering the full ML development lifecycle for medical devices: data quality, model design, transparency to users, and real-world performance monitoring.

title: OECD AI Principles (2019, updated 2024)
publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
summary: Intergovernmental soft-law principles — inclusive growth and well-being; human rights and fairness; transparency and explainability; robustness and safety; accountability — updated in 2024 to address generative AI.

title: Coalition for Health AI (CHAI) Trustworthy AI Framework
publisher: Coalition for Health AI (multi-stakeholder: health systems, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, academic medical centers)
summary: Multi-stakeholder industry framework (1,300+ member organizations) defining trustworthy health-AI criteria: usability and efficacy, safety and reliability, transparency, equity, and data security/privacy.

title: Global AI Governance in Healthcare: A Cross-Jurisdictional Regulatory Analysis
summary: Academic comparative analysis of how different jurisdictions (EU, US, others) regulate AI in healthcare, used here as research-tier evidence of cross-jurisdictional regulatory divergence rather than binding authority.

title: Dissecting Racial Bias in an Algorithm Used to Manage the Health of Populations
publisher: Science (peer-reviewed journal), Obermeyer, Powers, Vogeli & Mullainathan
summary: Landmark peer-reviewed study documenting that a widely used commercial healthcare risk-prediction algorithm exhibited significant racial bias because it used healthcare cost as a proxy for healthcare need. Cited here as research-tier evidence for the Bias/Fairness dimension in risk-scoring use cases.

title: Building Secure Foundations for Responsible AI in Healthcare with Microsoft
publisher: Microsoft (vendor blog, Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare)
summary: Vendor publication describing Microsoft's Responsible AI principles as applied to its healthcare cloud/AI products. Useful context on vendor commitments but carries no independent regulatory or standards authority — classified as Vendor Information, not a compliance obligation.

title: Epic Cognitive Computing Model Documentation ('Model Cards')
summary: Vendor-published transparency documentation for predictive models embedded in Epic's EHR (e.g., sepsis prediction, readmission risk). Used by health systems as an input to their own governance review, but is vendor material, not an independent standard or law.

title: AI Compliance Requirements for Healthcare Organizations: What You Need to Know
summary: General marketing/explainer blog content summarizing HIPAA and AI. Included deliberately as a General Web Content example so the application can show why this tier must never be treated as equivalent to the actual HIPAA regulatory text it discusses.

title: NYC Local Law 144 — Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDT)
publisher: New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
summary: Binding NYC law. Prohibits employers from using an Automated Employment Decision Tool (AEDT) for hiring or promotion unless it has passed an independent bias audit within the past year, with results published publicly. Enforcement tightened in 2026 following a December 2025 State Comptroller audit that found weak oversight.

title: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act (820 ILCS 42), as expanded by HB 3773
summary: Binding state law. Requires employers to notify candidates, explain how the AI works, and obtain consent before using AI to analyze video interviews, and to limit sharing/retention of recordings. HB 3773 (effective 1 Jan 2026) expanded coverage to AI used in recruitment, hiring, promotion, and other employment decisions generally, prohibiting discriminatory effect under the Illinois Human Rights Act.

title: Select Issues: Assessing Adverse Impact in Software, Algorithms, and Artificial Intelligence Used in Employment Selection Procedures Under Title VII
summary: Non-binding federal technical guidance applying Title VII's disparate-impact framework to algorithmic hiring tools (resume scanners, video-interview scoring, etc.). Clarifies an employer can be liable for a vendor-built tool's disparate impact even without intent to discriminate.

title: Identifying and Improving Disability Bias in GPT-Based Resume Screening
summary: Academic study documenting that GPT-based resume-screening prompts systematically ranked resumes disclosing a disability lower than otherwise-identical resumes. Research-tier evidence for the Bias/Fairness dimension in generative-AI hiring tools, not binding authority.

title: HireVue Press Release: External Bias Audit of Hiring Algorithms with DCI Consulting Group
summary: Vendor's own announcement of a third-party bias audit of its assessment algorithms. Included deliberately as Vendor Information: independent reporting on the same audits has noted the underlying results were less reassuring than the press release implied, illustrating why vendor claims should never substitute for independent review.

title: NYC Local Law 144 Compliance Guide 2026
summary: General marketing/explainer blog content summarizing Local Law 144 compliance steps. Included deliberately as a General Web Content example, distinct from the binding law text it summarizes.

title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
summary: The first global, intergovernmental standard on AI ethics, grounded in transparency, fairness, accountability, and human oversight, with concrete policy guidance across sectors. Used here as the universal, industry-agnostic baseline source since it explicitly applies 'across the full lifecycle of AI systems' regardless of sector.
